title: Credit epoch jump misapplied on Private deployments triggering throttled warmups
creator: Anjali Rao
description:
Incident summary:
During a sequence of private deployment restarts (customer-managed control plane), several customers experienced a sharp increase in 429s during service warmup periods. The pattern was repeatable after failover or config-applied restarts: the first 3–6 minutes of traffic to a freshly started host saw sustained throttles even though tenant credits showed available quota. Customers reported application timeouts and degraded UX for bursty onboarding traffic.

Timeline & observed behavior:
- 2026-02-28 03:12 UTC: Private control plane applied config patch to a small subset of nodes (staged rollout).
- 2026-02-28 03:17 UTC: Pager alerts for elevated 429s from impacted customers.
- 2026-02-28 03:35 UTC: On-call validated 429s correlated with dedicated/private hosts in the restarted cohort; token store showed credits present.
- 2026-02-28 04:02 UTC: Emergency mitigation deployed: short-circuit to bypass new epoch reconciliation for warmup traffic, which reduced 429s within 90s.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by investigation):
A race in epoch reconciliation logic for the per-tenant credit ledger caused an intermittent forward jump of the local epoch pointer when replaying persisted credit snapshots during startup. The jump effectively moved the sliding window forward without refilling real-time burst tokens, making the host believe the tenant had recently consumed its burst allowance. During warmup, requests were rejected until automatic refill logic (which uses wall-clock smoothing) caught up. This was only triggered on private deployments where snapshot replay is used and a specific sequence of control-plane restart + snapshot index advance occurred.

Why this was missed previously:
- Unit tests covered snapshot integrity but not cross-time epoch transitions during rapid restarts.
- E2E on private environments uses longer steady-state tests and didn’t simulate repeated restart sequences over compacted snapshots.

Immediate mitigations taken (post-detection):
- Hotfix (deployed 2026-02-28 04:02 UTC): bypass epoch-advance step for the first 5 minutes after host startup for all private/dedicated hosts (heuristic), allowing refill to saturate.
- Customer comms: informed impacted customers with steps to scale traffic and temporary workaround.

Proposed permanent fix (engineering plan):
1) Fix reconciliation logic to ensure epoch pointer advances only when snapshot delta semantics guarantee actual token consumption (ENSURE idempotent epoch application).
2) Add a startup state machine that differentiates persistent snapshot state vs in-memory consumption and forces an immediate reconciliation pass that refills burst tokens proportionally to time-since-last-consumption.
3) Extend snapshot format to include last_seen_wall_clock and a monotonic generation id to avoid out-of-order application.

Acceptance criteria (for deploy):
- Post-fix deterministic replay of snapshots does not cause transient negative-burst states during startup (validated in unit/integration tests).
- Simulated rapid restart + snapshot index advance test shows <1% of requests rejected during first 10 minutes in test harness across 10k tenants.
- No customer-facing 429 spikes in private staging over 48h canary.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Write targeted unit tests for epoch application logic (owner: Marco).
- Add a deterministic integration test that replays synthetic snapshot sequences under simulated wall-clock jumps (owner: Priya Shah).
- Canary rollout to 3 private customers (non-prod) for 24h, then broaden to 20 customers for 48h.
- Release in runtime-1.22 with feature flag disabled by default; enable for private deploys after canary verification.

Communication drafts / customer-facing language:
Short: "We identified and fixed a startup reconciliation bug that could cause transient request throttling after restarts. A fix is rolling out to private deployments; no action required. We apologize for the disruption and are monitoring."
Internal: include timeline, mitigations, and suggested support talking points (see Confluence link to postmortem doc).

Follow-ups / long-term work (postmortem action items):
- Postmortem write-up and blame-free RCA (owner: Anjali).
- Add synthetic chaos tests for private restart+snapshot sequences into CI (owner: Reliability team).
- Audit other epoch-based state machines for similar replay hazards (owner: Platform infra).
- Add metric for "startup_consumption_mismatch" to surface anomalies during warmup windows (owner: Observability).

Links & artifacts:
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1287 (hotfix branch).
- Incident runbook update: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/ENG-71234 (draft).
- Customer support thread examples: internal link (Slack) to #cust-esc-priv-startup.

Status & next steps:
- In Progress: implementing permanent fix + tests.
- Expected deploy to canary: 2026-03-17.
- Owner for rollout: Marco Delgado.

If you are triaging this ticket: please prioritize regression tests and the snapshot format change; escalate to Platform infra for design review on snapshot schema changes before code merge.
notes: PRs: runtime#1287 (hotfix), runtime#1299 (permanent fix). Monitoring dashboard updated: runtime/warmup-throttle-rate. Slack channel: #eng-incident-71234. QA to schedule chaos test for 2026-03-08.
